title: Exercise the remaining bot capabilities in a customer account
description:
**Phase 1 of 5.**

- **Blocked by:** ~~`chatticus-2f2d87` (F-computer)~~ — **cleared 2026-09-07.** F-computer confirmed refuse-not-fallback, then `chatticus-82dab7` deployed `ChatticusComputers` in the customer account and the **live cross-account `RunTask` passed**. A computer now starts in the customer account, so this card is ready.
- **Unblocks:** an honest pitch page, and any claim about what a customer gets

---

## Why this exists

`chatticus-b88c0a` proved the **backbone substrate** end to end in a customer account: Google sign-in, organization record, cross-account role with ExternalId, enablement, AWS home, and a completed turn (`pong`).

That is a real milestone and it is also **one capability out of many**. `pong` is a **computerless** turn — capability `cpu`. Every capability that touches the computer is unexercised in a customer account.

This card owns the rest of the matrix so the gaps are visible up front rather than found one at a time by a customer.

## Coverage after `b88c0a`

| Capability | Customer account | Evidence / gap |
|---|---|---|
| Google sign-in | **Proven** | `dev.chattic.us` |
| Organization record + `tenant_id` | **Proven** | Invisible in UI — `chatticus-9c8dbf` |
| Cross-account role, ExternalId, AssumeRole | **Proven** | `CREATE_COMPLETE`, template unmodified |
| Org enablement + AWS home | **Proven** | Operator deviation — `chatticus-070cb4` |
| Bot creation | Kernel only | No UI — `chatticus-7622fd` |
| **Computerless turn (`cpu`)** | **Proven** | `pong` |
| Computer start (cross-account RunTask) | **Unproven** | `chatticus-2f2d87` |
| Terminal / shell actions | **Not implemented** | No agent-facing tool exists. Confirmed 2026-09-07 — see below |
| Browser actions (Chromium) | **Unproven** | `browser_open` exists in the host executor, so this one is genuinely untested rather than absent |
| File actions (`/workspace`) | **Unproven, and predicted to fail** | See below |
| Approvals loop | **Unproven** | Consequential actions default to require-approval |
| Watch / takeover display | **Unproven** | |
| Spend ceiling enforcement | **Unproven** | The ceiling is what makes the price safe |
| Relocate / failover between hosts | **Unproven** | |

## One failure is predictable now, before running anything

**File actions will fail in a customer account as currently templated.**

`b88c0a` recorded that the published role CFN is scoped to `ChatticusComputers*` and **not** `ChatticusSnapshots`. `/workspace` depends on the S3 snapshot protocol for hydrate and publish — and per `chatticus-fbae4e` D3 (refuted 2026-09-07), that protocol is **permanent**, not a transitional artifact waiting for EFS. So a bot in a customer account cannot hydrate or publish `/workspace` without snapshot-bucket access the role does not grant.

That is a **template gap**, and by `chatticus-8a25af`'s rule a template change is **customer-visible** — an existing customer has to re-run it. Cheap now, expensive after the first customer.

**Decided 2026-09-07 — `chatticus-bb9084`.** The bucket lives in the **customer's own account** and is declared in the **customer-run published template**. Anthus `ChatticusSnapshots` serves Anthus-managed organizations only.

Creating it under the assumed role was ruled out on evidence, not preference: `infra/customer-role.yml` has **zero `s3:` actions**, and CloudFormation creates resources with the caller's permissions, so an `AWS::S3::Bucket` inside a Chatticus-deployed `ChatticusComputers` stack fails access-denied. The `ChatticusComputers*` filter scopes which *stacks* the role may touch, not which *resource types* it may create inside them. The template therefore changes either way — so the choice was made on merit: the customer can read a template-declared bucket before agreeing to it, and `s3:CreateBucket` stays off the Anthus role entirely.

This row stays blocked until `bb9084` lands, but it is now blocked on scoped work rather than an open question.

## Read the tool list before running the sweep (added 2026-09-07)

**The terminal row is not unproven — it does not exist.** The live retest of *"run `ls /workspace`"* returned *"I can't run shell commands directly in the household workspace"* with a **running computer** in the customer account. That answer is literally true:

```
chromium_action_executor.py:16
_SUPPORTED_TOOLS = frozenset({"browser_open", "request_computer_capability"})
```

The host executor supports **two tools**. No `run_shell`, `shell_exec`, `terminal_run` or `exec_command` exists anywhere in `python/src/chatticus/`. `request_computer_capability` with gate `workspace` is not a shell — the executor only opens Chromium, for the browser gate.

This closes the `STOP_NO_COMPUTER_TOOL` thread (`chatticus-5336ff`). It was never a prompting problem, never a grant denial, and not an escalation defect. **The capability has no tool.**

**Note the documentation gap:** `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` lists `terminal` among worker capabilities and says the computer image contains *"a shell"*. Both are true of the image and neither is reachable by an agent.

**Before running any row below, read the tool list first.** *Unproven* and *unimplemented* cost very different amounts — one is a verification, the other is a feature. Enumerating which capabilities have agent-facing tools is a ten-minute code read; discovering it one row at a time through live AWS runs is the expensive way to learn the same thing.

## Sequence

1. `chatticus-2f2d87` **F-computer** — a computer starts at all. Everything else is blocked on it.
2. ~~**Terminal**~~ — **build, not verify.** No tool exists; this is a feature. Then **browser**, which does have `browser_open` and is genuinely untestable-until-tried.
3. **File actions** — blocked on `chatticus-bb9084` (bucket in the customer-run template). Until it lands, expect access-denied: the role has no S3 permissions.
4. **Approvals** — a consequential action pauses and resumes correctly across the account boundary.
5. **Spend ceiling** — enforcement is what makes the floated price safe.
6. **Relocate / failover** — last; the least likely to be exercised by an early customer.

Stop and record at the first failure in each row rather than pushing through. A labeled stop is a result.

## Record

Same discipline as `b88c0a`: wiki runbook with placeholders, real ids in gitignored `AGENTS.local.md`, every deviation labeled. Add elapsed time per capability — the ~19 min provisioning figure covers **none** of this.

## Done when

Each row above is proven, or has a recorded failure with a decision about what changes — template, infrastructure, or product scope.

## File actions: the bucket question is decided (2026-09-07)

The predicted file-actions failure now has an answer.

**Snapshot packs live in the customer's own AWS account, and the bucket is created in advance by the published CloudFormation template.** Anthus's `ChatticusSnapshots` bucket serves Anthus-managed organizations only. Filed as `chatticus-bb9084`.

Chosen over having Chatticus create the bucket under the assumed role because the customer can review a template-declared bucket before running it, and because it keeps `s3:CreateBucket` off the role entirely — a permission that would fail `8a25af`'s *"why does an agent product need this"* test.

The **file actions** row here stays blocked until that lands, and it is now blocked on a scoped piece of work rather than an open question.

comments.text:
## Two things above are now settled — do not treat them as open (2026-09-07)

**1. The bucket question is decided.** The earlier comment on this card reads *"whoever creates that bucket (template vs assumed-role `ChatticusComputers` — F-computer will say)."* F-computer did not decide it; the role file did.

`infra/customer-role.yml` has **zero `s3:` actions**, and CloudFormation creates resources with the caller's permissions, so an `AWS::S3::Bucket` inside a Chatticus-deployed `ChatticusComputers` stack fails access-denied. Since the template has to change either way, the choice was made on merit: **the bucket is declared in the customer-run published template** (`chatticus-bb9084`), where the customer can read it before agreeing, and `s3:CreateBucket` never goes on the Anthus role.

**2. This card is no longer blocked.** `chatticus-82dab7` closed after the **live cross-account `RunTask` passed** on development. A computer starts in the customer account. Terminal and browser rows can proceed now; **file actions** wait on `bb9084`.

## Suggested first probe

The prompt that produced *"I can't run shell commands directly in the household workspace"* failed with `STOP_NO_COMPUTER_TOOL`, which was plausibly downstream of there being no `ChatticusComputers` stack to start. That is now fixed and **nobody has rechecked**.

Re-running it is a cheap, high-value first step. Use a probe that does **not** touch `/workspace` — `echo hello` or `uname -a` — so a genuine escalation bug is not masked by the S3 gap that `bb9084` will fix. If it still refuses with a working computer behind it, that isolates a real escalation defect and deserves its own card; if it works, the symptom closes with no further work.
